card-prompt.purpose: Primary retrieval question in study column; SwiftUI .largeTitle

card-secondary.purpose: Supporting card content beneath the answer; SwiftUI .title2

ui-display.purpose: The one number a pane exists to deliver, today the scope home due headline; SwiftUI .title2 bold with monospaced digits. Bold rather than larger, because sizes above this belong to the card.

ui-title.purpose: Pane titles and sheet headlines; SwiftUI .title2 semibold. Emphasis here is weight and space, never card sizes.

ui-row-meta.purpose: Sidebar scope row counts under the name; SwiftUI .caption

motion.name: reveal-crossfade
motion.purpose: Answer reveal in study view; disabled when Reduce Motion is on — use instant cut.

motion.name: grade-submit
motion.purpose: No animation between cards; swap content immediately to preserve study flow.

platformNotes.macOS14: Semantic system colors; standard NavigationSplitView materials.
platformNotes.macOS26: Optional Liquid Glass on sidebar and toolbar only; study content stays opaque.
platformNotes.iOSFuture: Stack navigation; bottom-fixed grade bar; 44pt touch targets.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Study, Show Answer, Done, and an empty state's single call to action. SwiftUI .borderedProminent with app tint; .controlSize(.large) in empty states.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #4A6FA5; color: #fff; padding: 8px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 8px; font: 400 13px/1.4 -apple-system, 'SF Pro', system-ui; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #3d5f8f; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #4A6FA5; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Grade Button
components.css: .ds-btn-grade { background: transparent; color: #1d1d1f; padding: 6px 14px; border: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.15); border-radius: 6px; font: 400 13px/1.4 -apple-system, 'SF Pro', system-ui; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-grade:hover { background: rgba(0,0,0,0.04); } .ds-btn-grade:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #4A6FA5; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Study Reading Column
components.description: Centered card stage, max 600pt. Prompt, divider, answer — no shadow box.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-study-column { max-width: 600px; margin: 0 auto; text-align: center; padding: 24px 32px; } .ds-prompt { font: 400 34px/1.25 -apple-system, 'SF Pro', system-ui; margin: 0 0 24px; } .ds-divider { border: none; border-top: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.12); margin: 24px 0; } .ds-answer { font: 400 28px/1.3 -apple-system, 'SF Pro', system-ui; color: rgba(0,0,0,0.85); margin: 0; }

components.name: Scope Home Summary
components.description: Default detail pane for a sidebar scope: the due count as a bold display headline, one prominent Study action, a neutral typographic card-state breakdown under a quiet group label, and a secondary link into browse mode. The scope name lives in the window title, not above the headline — the headline has nothing to compete with, and everything below it is quieter than a section heading. No card type sizes, no colored stat pills, no progress rings.

components.css: .ds-scope-home { max-width: 600px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 24px; padding: 24px 32px; } .ds-due-block { padding-bottom: 8px; } .ds-due-headline { font: 700 22px/1.25 -apple-system, 'SF Pro', system-ui; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; margin: 0 0 12px; } .ds-group-label { font: 400 13px/1.3 -apple-system, 'SF Pro', system-ui; color: rgba(0,0,0,0.55); margin: 0 0 12px; } .ds-card-states { display: flex; gap: 32px; margin: 0; } .ds-card-states dd { font: 600 17px/1.3 -apple-system, 'SF Pro', system-ui; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; margin: 0; } .ds-card-states dt { font: 400 13px/1.3 -apple-system, 'SF Pro', system-ui; color: rgba(0,0,0,0.55); } .ds-scope-link { font: 400 13px/1.3 -apple-system, 'SF Pro', system-ui; color: #4A6FA5; }

components.name: Browse Table Row
components.description: One row of the browse-mode table: prompt plus scheduling state. The Answer column exists but ships hidden through TableColumnCustomization, so opening the library never spoils a card; revealing it is a Library menu command with a shortcut, and the choice persists across browse sessions.

components.name: Sidebar Scope Row
components.description: Deck or scope row in the sidebar: name over a due/item metadata line. Selection is the system List highlight; no custom row background.

components.name: Error Banner
components.description: Inline study error with icon; never color alone.

narrative.overview: NeoAnki2 should feel like a well-lit desk: one open page (the card), a tidy shelf of decks to the side, and almost nothing else competing for attention. Selecting a scope answers what to study now; enumerating items is a deliberate browse mode you ask for. Platform-native restraint and content-forward layout. The card is the only hero per screen.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Custom accent color appears only on primary forward actions (Study, Show Answer, Done on completion, and an empty state's single call to action). Browse mode gets no prominent accent button.

rules.name: The No Gamification Palette Rule
rules.body: Do not introduce streak orange, achievement gold, or chart rainbow colors.

rules.name: The Card Type Scale Rule
rules.body: Only card prompt uses .largeTitle; only card answer uses .title. UI chrome never borrows card sizes — the scope home's due headline earns emphasis from weight and space instead.

rules.name: The Dynamic Type Rule
rules.body: Use semantic SwiftUI text styles — never hard-coded point sizes in production views.

rules.name: The Split-First Rule
rules.body: Study never returns to a sheet modal on Mac. Detail pane owns the session.

rules.name: The Reading Measure Rule
rules.body: Card text and prose live in a centered column capped at 600pt. Dense tables in browse mode take the full detail width.

rules.name: The Study-Forward Default Rule
rules.body: The detail pane's default branch answers what to do now. A bare list of everything is never the landing state for a scope.

rules.name: The No Answers by Default Rule
rules.body: No library surface reveals an item's answer without an explicit request. Browse mode ships the Answer column hidden; row subtitles never carry it. The reveal is a menu command with a shortcut and it persists, so the default is considered rather than a restriction nobody can lift.

rules.name: The Flat Study Stage Rule
rules.body: The study card is not a boxed card with shadow. Divider and typography only.

rules.name: The Platform Shape Rule
rules.body: Use system control geometry; custom radii only for future media containers.

dos: Do keep one primary action visible per study phase
Do expose keyboard paths and document in Grade Help
Do test Light, Dark, and Increased Contrast
Do adopt Liquid Glass on sidebar/toolbar for macOS 26 with opaque study content
donts: Don't gamify with streaks, XP, or progress rings
Don't put shadows, gradients, or glass on card content
Don't use display serifs or cute illustration styles
Don't copy Anki density or Quizlet game UI
Don't show scheduling stats during active review — the scope home is where they belong, read before a session rather than during one
Don't reveal an item's answer anywhere in the library without being asked
